The extension search is scanning the workspace instead of the extensions folder.

pyproject.toml currently lacks a build-system and project scripts. uv run can execute Python files directly without installation. However, [project.scripts] requires an installable project. Need to determine if the project needs a build backend to support this.

IOGraph uses uv and has a lock file. Without an explicit build-system, uv may treat the project as virtual or default to setuptools. Virtual projects typically cannot support [project.scripts].

Checking uv.lock and the current run command. For the build script, PyInstaller is not a native console entry point, so options include adding an `iograph-build` wrapper script or calling the PowerShell script directly from tasks.json. The existing `scripts/build_windows.ps1` conflicts with `uv-launcher generate`, which would create its own launcher scripts. A Python wrapper module like `iograph/build.py` with a `main()` function is cleaner than wrapping the PowerShell script for `uv run iograph-build`. Hatch or uv scripts are also being considered.

Checking whether uv 0.9+ supports `[tool.uv.scripts]` as an alternative to `[project.scripts]`. Hatch also offers a comparable scripts section. The existing project already uses `[project.scripts]` with uv-launcher, so that pattern is likely the right fit.

Checking the cdanniel.vscode-custom-buttons extension and its commands.json format. Verifying whether it is installed. Also reviewing stream_viewer as a reference from uv-launcher examples.

The CI release uses a folder distribution, not a single-file executable. The `IOGraph.spec` file is Windows-oriented and references Windows paths. Adding `[project.scripts]` entries requires a build backend, which the current `pyproject.toml` does not have.

Without a build backend, `uv` treats the project as virtual-only and does not install `[project.scripts]`. Adding `hatchling` as the build backend and enabling `tool.uv.package = true` will allow the console scripts to be registered. This is cleaner than using setuptools.

I will skip adding `[project.scripts]` to keep the change minimal. The buttons can simply run `uv run python run_iograph.py` and `powershell scripts/build_windows.ps1`. I still need to confirm which Custom Buttons extension they use.

Checking git ignore rules with a negation pattern.

Confirmed `.vscode/` files are untracked and visible. The negation rule overrides the `.vscode/*` ignore pattern.

The `.vscode/*` pattern ignores directory contents without blocking the folder itself. This avoids a gitignore gotcha where a directory-level ignore prevents git from checking inside it.

- **Build IOGraph exe** → `scripts/build_windows.ps1` (default build task)
- Status-bar buttons are in [`IOGraph.code-workspace`](c:\Users\pho\repos\EmotivEpoc\ACTIVE_DEV\IOGraph\IOGraph.code-workspace) and [`.vscode/settings.json`](c:\Users\pho\repos\EmotivEpoc\ACTIVE_DEV\IOGraph\.vscode\settings.json). They call `workbench.action.tasks.runTask`.
- [`.vscode/extensions.json`](c:\Users\pho\repos\EmotivEpoc\ACTIVE_DEV\IOGraph\.vscode\extensions.json) recommends `jkearins.action-buttons-ext`.

Install the Action Buttons extension if the status-bar buttons are missing, then reload the window. After that, **Launch IOGraph** and **Build IOGraph exe** should appear in the status bar and under **Terminal → Run Task**.
